security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, placeholder credential names, official links, and benign prose. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found. The skill still presents privileged Azure operations that can affect cost, access, and service availability.

remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before mutations, and show the target subscription, resource group, capacity, region, administrator list, and SKU.
Prefer managed identity or workload identity. Never print client secrets, store them in source control, or include them in generated examples.

content.value_statement: Managing Microsoft Fabric capacity through Azure Resource Manager requires precise SDK workflows. This skill provides .NET guidance for authentication, provisioning, scaling, suspension, deletion, and status checks.
actual_capabilities: Provide installation guidance for the Azure Resource Manager Fabric SDK and Azure Identity packages.
Authenticate ARM clients with DefaultAzureCredential and retrieve the active Azure subscription.
Create, retrieve, update, suspend, resume, list, and delete Fabric capacities.
Check capacity name availability and list supported SKUs by subscription or capacity.
Handle long-running operations, provisioning states, and common ARM request failures.
Explain management-plane scope, resource hierarchy, SDK types, and regional constraints.
limitations: Covers Fabric capacity management only, not workspaces, lakehouses, warehouses, or data items.
Requires valid Azure authentication, permissions, subscription access, regional availability, and quota.
Package versions, API behavior, SKU availability, and pricing can change after publication.
Examples can modify or delete billable cloud resources and require environment-specific testing.

use_cases.title: Provision Fabric capacity
use_cases.description: Generate a .NET workflow that authenticates, validates inputs, creates a Fabric capacity, and waits for provisioning to finish.

use_cases.title: Automate capacity lifecycle
use_cases.description: Build repeatable routines for listing, scaling, suspending, resuming, and deleting capacities with state checks.

use_cases.title: Review SDK integration
use_cases.description: Check a C# implementation for correct ARM types, asynchronous operations, error handling, and management-plane boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Set up Fabric management
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to set up a .NET application for Microsoft Fabric capacity management using DefaultAzureCredential and my Azure subscription.

prompt_templates.title: Provision a capacity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C# workflow for capacity [name] in [resource group], using [region], [SKU], and [administrator UPNs].

prompt_templates.title: Manage the capacity lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that lists capacities, scales [capacity] to [SKU], suspends it when idle, and resumes it after state validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review resilient automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Fabric automation for idempotency, least privilege, long-running operations, retries, quota failures, and guarded deletion. Explain every recommended change.

output_examples.input: I need an F64 development capacity in West US 2.
output: Validate that F64 is available in West US 2 and confirm subscription quota.
Authenticate with DefaultAzureCredential and select the intended subscription and resource group.
Check global name availability before starting the create or update operation.
Confirm administrators, tags, expected cost, and the final provisioning state.

output_examples.input: How should I stop charges while a capacity is unused?
output_examples.output: Retrieve the target capacity, confirm its identity and current state, then suspend it. Verify the Suspended state before reporting completion.

output_examples.input: My capacity update returned an Azure request error.
output: Capture the status code, Azure error code, and correlation details without exposing credentials.
Treat conflicts, invalid configuration, permission failures, and quota failures as distinct cases.
Recheck the resource state before retrying any operation.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with least-privilege Azure roles and avoid hardcoded secrets.
Confirm subscription, resource group, capacity name, region, SKU, administrators, and cost before mutations.
Wait for long-running operations when required, handle ARM errors, and verify the final provisioning state.
anti_patterns: Do not use this SDK for Fabric workspaces, lakehouses, warehouses, or data-plane items.
Do not delete, suspend, resume, scale, or reassign administrators without explicit target confirmation.
Do not assume that a SKU, quota, package version, or API behavior is identical across regions and subscriptions.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Microsoft Fabric capacity resources through the Azure Resource Manager management plane.

faq.question: Does it manage Fabric workspaces and data items?
faq.answer: No. Use the Microsoft Fabric REST API or a supported data-plane SDK for those resources.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity, workload identity, developer credentials, or a carefully protected service principal.

faq.question: Can it create and delete capacities?
faq.answer: Yes. These operations require Azure permissions and can affect billing, access, and service availability.

faq.question: How should long-running operations be handled?
faq.answer: Wait for completion when later steps depend on the result. Otherwise, start the operation and poll its status safely.

faq.question: Are the listed versions and SKUs always current?
faq.answer: No. Verify package versions, regional SKU availability, quotas, API behavior, and pricing against current Microsoft documentation.
